/config settings panel: tab row, rounded ╭─╮ search box, scrolling list, key-hint footer The generic menu grammar finds its region top by walking up from the footer for the nearest rule or box border within REGION_SCAN_WINDOW (30 rows, menu.ts). Here that rule is the search box's ╰─╯ bottom border: 24 rows above the footer at 82 columns, and 32 above it on a 120-column live capture (2026-09-22), whose taller list fits 30 setting rows between the two. Past the window the walk finds nothing, detectMenuRegion returns null, and the screen falls to the unread-dialog card instead. A fix has to stop measuring the region top in a fixed row count — size the window to the pane's own height, or anchor on the panel's tab row rather than the nearest rule — and it must still decline a borderless buffer, which is what the bound is there for. [2026-10-06, Claude Code 2.1.291: this file keeps its 2.1.278 bytes because other suites pin them; the 2.1.291 capture of the same state is claude-lab--menu-config-panel-v2291--w82.txt.]
entries.knownKeyGap: The footer names 'Enter/↓ to select' as ONE compound token, and menuKeyFor takes a single key token, so Enter and Down are dropped and the menu offers Up and Escape alone. Candidate grammar: a compound-token reader for key-hint footers, which the '↑/↓' form of the same hint needs too.

Candidate grammar: a key-hint footer reader that rejoins a footer's wrapped continuation rows before parsing them, so a narrow pane reads the same keys as a wide one.
